species.real: Jersey and Guernsey are not part of the UK. They are Crown Dependencies with their own parliaments and laws, though the King is their head of state.
species.name: Crockling

dex.text: A small brown crock with a lid that rattles when it is happy, and it is happy most of the time. Sits very still all night, then smells wonderful by morning.
dex.fact: The Jersey bean crock is a slow-baked stew of haricot beans, pork and a pig's trotter. It was traditionally taken to the village baker on Saturday night, to cook in the cooling bread oven, and fetched home after church on Sunday.

species.real: The islands have teased each other for centuries: Guernsey people are nicknamed donkeys, and Jersey people crapauds, which is Norman French for toads.
species.name: Beancrock

dex.text: Big, brown and slow, with a cloth tied round its lid and a trotter hanging out of the top. It will not be hurried and it will not be put down, and the whole street knows when it is nearly ready.
dex.fact: Guernsey has its own bean jar, made the same slow way with beans and pork. Both islands' versions were once the Sunday dinner, left to cook in the baker's oven while the family was at church.
